text:
Alex (oncall): :rotating_light: Pager alert — multiple inference pods on cluster-prod-2 have OOM killed and then the node degraded to NotReady. Seeing repeated driver resets (Xid 31 / 43) in dmesg. Paging SRE.
Jasmin (sre): copying from metrics — ECC correctable count spiked on gpu-node-17, then nv-host reset and containers crashed. Pods show exit code 137 and container logs truncated.
Alex (oncall): @here taking first look. Are there any customers currently impacted? Telemetry shows an increase in 5xx for /v1/generate on the hosted API cluster region-us-east.
Customer Success: we've got two customer support tickets reporting request failures and increased latency — flagging high-touch customers CUST-491 and CUST-502.
OpsBot: Incident created: #INC-2026-211, severity P1. Notifying infra and runtime teams.
Rohan (infra): I can confirm node flapping across a handful of hosts in the us-east pool. Kernel logs show GPU ECC correctable errors followed by nv-peer or nv-host resets. Possibly thermal or board-level. I'll start isolating nodes.
Maya (eng-runtime): From the runtime side, we've observed KV cache corruption symptoms — attempts to restore context for long sequences cause memory spikes then the GPU driver drops. Short-term mitigation: switch affected model pools to lower-seqlen model variants and disable long-context caching for new requests.
Jasmin (sre): Suggested mitigation plan in order: 1) cordon+drain suspicious nodes, 2) move traffic via routing policy to dedicated fallback pool, 3) reduce model batch size and disable prefix caching for in-flight sessions, 4) coordinate driver collection and possible node reboot. Doing step 1 now.
Alex (oncall): Executing drain on gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-21: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-node-17` — will watch for evictions. ETA 3-4 minutes.
Rohan (infra): Starting hardware telemetry capture and pushing NVidia logs to /var/log/gpu-maint: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.free,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1 > /var/log/gpu-maint/gpu-node-17-sample.log`.
Maya (eng-runtime): Temporary runtime config I'd like applied cluster-wide until we stabilize:
```
# runtime override (short-term)
batching.max_tokens=512
kv_cache.enabled=false
model.variant.fallback=true
```
This will lower memory pressure. Can infra apply via configmap?
Rohan (infra): Applying configmap rollout to the impacted daemonset now. Pushing to canary nodes first.
Jasmin (sre): After drain, node reports clean but host driver still shows recent Xid 31 events. Recommend soft-reload of driver and NV persistence mode check. Rohan can attempt `nvidia-modprobe -u` and `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` if safe.
Rohan (infra): Will do a driver soft-reload on gpu-node-21 first. If host reports sustained ECC counts, we'll schedule a hard reboot. Performing: `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` (watching for kernel oops). Rolling now.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: configmap runtime-override applied to 3/3 targeted nodes (canary complete).
Alex (oncall): Runtime metrics show tail latency drop after limiting batch size, and errors on /v1/generate falling by ~60%. Good sign.
Customer Success: Notifying CUST-491 and CUST-502 that we're investigating and routing them to fallback region; providing ETA 30m for full mitigation.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also recommend setting autoscaler cooldown higher temporarily to avoid thrashing as nodes drain. I'll open a PR for autoscaler bump.
Jasmin (sre): Observed one node with repeated ECC corrections — suspect board-level degradation. Rohan, can we cordon the rest of the nodes older than 2022-10 and shift workload to newer hardware pool (gpu-newpool)?
Rohan (infra): Starting migration to gpu-newpool. Creating node selector override for the failing deployment groups, will shift traffic over the next 15 mins.
Alex (oncall): Quick diagnostic logs pasted for context:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=0, Channel 00000003
[ 1234.568010] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.570000] docker: containerd: task killed: signal=9
```
Maya (eng-runtime): That Xid 31 pattern matches previous driver-reset cascade we saw last quarter. We should enable a short-circuit fallback in the router: after N failed requests from a node, mark node as degraded and avoid routing to models pinned there.
Jasmin (sre): Agree. I've added a temporary route rule in the router: `degraded_threshold=5` and `route_away=true` for nodes with driver resets. OpsBot applied it.
OpsBot: Router rule updated: degraded_threshold=5, route_away=true.
Customer Success: Customer CUST-491 acknowledged, appreciated proactive routing. CUST-502 requests incident updates every 15 minutes.
Rohan (infra): After soft-reload, gpu-node-21 shows ECC correctables still increasing slowly — scheduling a scheduled reboot for low-impact window in 10 minutes. Marking node for hardware inspection post-reboot.
Alex (oncall): For the incident timeline and comms: I'll prepare a short post to status.redwood.ai: note transient GPU driver resets in us-east, partial outage for hosted inference, fallback routing in place, expected recovery in 30–60 minutes.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also enabling lower-precision quantization fallback for a subset of requests to reduce memory footprint (will only affect non-sensitive customer models). Rolling now.
Jasmin (sre): Telemetry shows error rate stabilizing after move to gpu-newpool and driver reloads. Still seeing occasional Xid 43 on one host — keeping cordon until inspection.
Alex (oncall): Summarizing actions taken so far: 1) cordoned/drained suspected nodes; 2) soft-reloaded driver on canary, scheduled reboots for persistently noisy hosts; 3) applied runtime overrides to reduce batch/cache pressure; 4) routed traffic to newer hardware and fallback pools; 5) customer notifications and status page update; 6) hardware ticket created for on-site inspection.
Rohan (infra): Hardware ticket created: HT-9843 — vendor dispatch requested. Attaching logs and dmesg snapshots to ticket.
Customer Success: Customers updated on status page. CUST-502 accepted 15m cadence; they're fine with fallback but want root cause when available.
Maya (eng-runtime): Next steps: collect full GPU driver logs (dmesg + nvidia-smi -q) from the effected hosts, run extended memtest64 for the GPU memory, and reproduce under a throttled KV-cache workload in staging. I'll coordinate with infra.
Jasmin (sre): On-call handoff note for next rotation: continue to monitor ECC correctable trend, keep dev overrides for 1 hour, and follow hardware ticket. I'll prepare a short runbook update with these steps.
Alex (oncall): Thanks team. If the node reboots come back clean, we'll start uncordoning one at a time and observe for 30m before returning routing to normal. Moving to incident summary channel in 15m.
PagerDuty: Acknowledged. Incident severity downgraded to P2 after stabilization of error rate. Closing on-call paging loop.
OpsBot: Incident #INC-2026-211 — current status: stabilizing. Logs archived to s3://redwood-incidents/2026/INC-2026-211/
Maya (eng-runtime): Leaving trace of the runtime mitigation commands used in case we need to revert:
```
# applied overrides
./rctl set batching.max_tokens=512
./rctl set kv_cache.enabled=false
./rctl rollout restart runtime-pool
```
Jasmin (sre): Final note: root cause hypothesis — failing GPU memory modules causing correctable ECC surges that lead to NV driver resets and downstream container OOMs. Hardware verification required to confirm. Will update when vendor inspection complete.
Alex (oncall): Closing thread for now. Will reopen if new Xid events appear. Thanks all :thumbsup:
